uncited: *   **Degenerate Input:** If a mesh-cell has zero ray-segments, it contributes zero load and zero communication.
Assigns each mesh-cell to the processor with the maximum local ray-segment count, minimizing communication volume but ignoring load balance.
Assigns mesh-cells in decreasing order of global load to the minimally loaded processor.
*   **Time Complexity:** The parallel pre-computation requires $O(N \cdot P)$ work for local traversal and $O(N \log P)$ or $O(N)$ for global reduction depending on the communication topology.
The assignment loop is $O(N \cdot P)$ if finding the min/max load naively, or $O(N \log P)$ with a heap.
*   **When not to use:** If communication is negligible compared to computation, pure BFD may be simpler.
